Hi! 

First off, thanks for coming to our wedding! This is an app called __WIGI__, short for _"Wherever I'm going, I'm happy you're coming"_. It's a line from our first dance song, _Pretty Boy_ by The Neighbourhood. This is a list of locations Alyssa and I have been throughout our time together. Not exhaustive, but I did my best to include everywhere we took pictures. This is the first card of 80-or-so locations. You can swipe through the cards horizontally (swipe left!), and you can swipe through the pictures on each individual card. Each card has a short blurb about the location, and below that is an interactive Google Maps pin of the location itself. Scroll through the cards and travel with us!

For the programmers here -- the source code can be found on [GitHub](https://github.com/ajsampang67/wigi). It's a pretty simple widget-based app written in Dart with Flutter. Very similar to Javascript with React Native. Highly recommend! The app took me about a month to create, from knowing nothing about Dart/Flutter to what you're looking at now. It's deployed on an EC2 instance using docker-compose, served via nginx webserver alongside my personal website.

This first pin below is Jade Mountain, our honeymoon destination!

Welcome to our wedding venue, The BRIX on the Fox! This building is originally a condensed milk factory, built in 1880. In 2018, Rob and Tone Gorman renovated the space into a one-stop wedding venue overlooking the Fox River.

In May of 2022, Alyssa and I were in the middle of our venue tours. The BRIX was the third spot we'd visit, but the last one we'd need. Alyssa and I got in the car and discussed how this was the first venue we could picture getting married. On the trip from The BRIX to the next venue, _Pretty Boy_ by The Neighbourhood came on, and we immediately knew it would be our first dance song.

The Brix is a pretty cool venue. Rob and Tone were purposeful in their renovation of The Brix. The acoustics of the Two-Sixty are targeted such that the dance floor will BOOM without flooding too much noise into the seating area. The ceilings are set up with infrastructure for separating the room into areas for the ceremony, and then shortly after for cocktail hour and reception. Rob and Tone showed their drive to make a beautiful wedding space, and in turn, made the decision easy to make our love official in this space.

Alyssa and I met at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign. Here we took a GenEd, Latin American Studies together. We met when our mutual friends sat together, where I took the empty seat next to Alyssa. We chatted through the class and parted ways. A few days later, I go over to my friend's apartment to grab some of my beers from their fridge and lo-and-behold! Alyssa was there! She was friends with my neighboring apartment as they were both in UIUC's nursing program.

From there, we were lucky enough to hang out more and get to know one another. We went on lunch dates and study dates. We spent time at the Underground Library enjoying Bad and Boujee and Pillow Talk music videos on repeat. We spent hours watching the Jimmy Neutron Movie while writing an essay about Latin American coups. We enjoyed our midnight cheese snacks and insomnia cookies. We worked hard and played harder, and somehow came out with our degrees!

The UI Ice Arena was a pretty regular place for the two of us. We were at UIUC right at the tail end of the Blackhawks' run, resulting in myself having some interest in learning how to skate in hockey skates. Alyssa, more of a natural, had 14 years of figure skating experience already under her belt! The pictures you see above are July of 2016 from our first ice skating date, and again in December of 2017 for a special holiday-themed skate

Chicago is where Alyssa and I had our first _real real_ date. Ally had told me that despite her living in Chicago, she never went to any of the tourist spots. She'd never been to The Bean, gone to the top of the Sears Tower, or ridden the Ferris wheel at Navy Pier! I grabbed us some disposable cameras and took her on a tourist date around the city. The first few photos you see are just that; they're a bit vintage looking from the cheap film of the disposable. 

Other than that, it's only natural we'd visit the city fairly often. We liked to go in the winter to visit the Christkindlmarket, do some Macy's window shopping, and take some pictures with the big tree.

Curtis is a nice farm out in Champaign. Alyssa is a real Autumn Ally and makes sure we visit a pumpkin patch every year. They've got a big chair, petting zoo, and delicious hot apple cider! 

_"I like it! We go there a lot when we were young spring chickens, and I like it. What are you saying about it Alf? That you like it?"_ - Alyssa Nicole
December of 2016 was the first holiday season we spent together. Enjoy a quick couple of pictures of Alyssa spending time with the Sampang's on Christmas!

Just after the New Year of 2017, Alyssa got us some Blackhawks tickets for our first NHL game together! This is the day we first consider ourselves "official", January 5th of 2016. Since then we celebrate every 5th of the month as "Buns Day" (like pork bun, because Ally is cute like a pork bun). We make sure to have a nice dinner date, or watch a movie, or at very least fit in an extra face kiss!

On this day I actually accidentally threw out our Hawks tickets before the game! This was back when they __only__ accepted paper tickets. The hotel had already taken away our trash, and I begged the front desk to dig through the trash and retrieve it for us. Lucky for us, they called back half an hour later, and found it! Alyssa and I attended the game and had a fantastic time. Patrick Kane scored the GWG in OT on a breakaway as Alyssa took a bathroom break.

Beckwith is a residential community at UIUC dedicated to students with severe physical disabilities, in which Beckwith assists these residents in the transition to independent living. Alyssa worked as a CNA assisting students with some of their daily tasks, such as getting ready for bed or preparing meals for the day. 

The photos in this slide are from the yearly Beckwith semi-formal 2018 and 2019! We got to dress up with a theme and have dinner with everyone. The people Alyssa got to work with were always so sweet, Lauren was a huge Panic! at the Disco fan like myself, and our good friend Danny who always made us laugh went on to become a successful lawyer after school!

I hate rollercoasters, but Alyssa loves them! Somehow she got me to go along with her in May of 2017 and I went on _almost_ every ride with her. I will never go on giant drops, and I hate wooden roller coasters. Alyssa had a great time though.

_"Aj hated every second of it"_ - Alyssa Nicole

In the summer of 2017 I got my first "real job" in the form of an internship at Nutanix, a cloud computing company providing servers and software for cloud computing. Alyssa was sweet enough to take the time to come out east and visit me! Here we went to the Sarah P. Duke Gardens, a restaurant hosting a wall-art coloring book event, and a benefit dinner for Durham's _Families Moving Forward_ organization.

Everyone knows the Christkindlmarket in Chicago! Alyssa and I try to go every year. The pictures you see here are from 2017, 2019, and 2021. So we really have a 50% success rate. We tried to go this past year, 2022, but the line was far too long! We opted instead to take a walk through the Millennium Park and grab some sushi at a restaurant nearby. The pictures from that date can be found on the Chicago slide.

Sakanaya is one of the nicer sushi places out in Champaign. We didn't come here often, just to celebrate bigger events. This last picture was probably the last time we went, Alyssa's birthday in 2018! On my sushi rankings list, this falls in the "B Tier" (which, I still like a lot!).

Riu Santa Fe was actually mine and Alyssa's very first all-inclusive vacation and it was AWESOME! Big thank you to our friend Lea who not only accompanied us on this trip, but really spearheaded the idea. We had a great time with our friends, we got some delicious drinks and laid out on the beach. Alyssa and I decided to go out on an excursion to swim with some whale sharks near La Paz, check it out next!

La Paz was a really cool visit for us! The main event of the trip was swimming with some whale sharks. We threw on fins and wetsuits and got diving! This small charter boat drove us to an area near whale sharks, and we just dove in and swam alongside them. It was horrifying and fascinating all at once. 
Before some hard swimming against the currents, we went to the city of La Paz! Here we did some shopping and got lunch. It was a nice catered lunch the whale-shark-diving group had organized for us. This was the first of many south-of-the-US excursions to come!

Back in the US and still in our summer after graduating from UIUC, we wanted to continue on our little adventures. We were craving a spot to hike, and Ally had the great idea of hiking Starved Rock! I had only been there as a kid to go fishing, so although I've been here tens of times, it was really cool to get a completely new look at the place. Alyssa took us to some familiar trails she had gone through before, and we got some nice pictures out of it.
Brookfield Zoo is solid, but admittedly Alyssa and I have a bad habit of going a bit too late when all the animals are asleep! But enjoy some pictures of us with the free-roaming peacocks!

In June of 2018, Ally and I went up to Ann Arbor, Michigan so I could show her around the city and visit my sister. We had a great time kayaking and checking out the local museum. The campus had a festival at the time as well, so we got to hangout on the quad with some drinks and live music!

column4: As Ally and I finished up school and moved back home, we were no longer near our regular Curtis pumpkin patch and had to find a new one! Luckily enough, Bengston's was nearby and became our norm. Here we have pictures from Octobers of 2018 and 2019. Look how much we grew in one year!!! wild

In October of 2018 we decided to visit Mickey's Halloween Party at Disneyland! Despite hating rollercoasters, I actually do love Space Mountain. One of my all-time favorite pics of the two of us is on the third slide here -- wild excitement coming down from Ghost Galaxy! We got our matching shirts and visited Mickey's House. Alyssa played the piano for Mr. Mouse. A very successful visit!

Alyssa and I were actually in California primarily due to my own work -- Liferay had flown all the employees down for a conference. Talking with all the employees, obviously someone had to know the best sushi spot in town! One of the highest references was Ohshima sushi, which we landed on as it was so close to Disneyland Park. This was our first real Omakase experience, and it SLAPPED. This sushi restaurant topped our rankings list until just recently -- when Chicago's BoozeBox dethroned them. Still, Ohshima is no joke, and we'll definitely be back in the future!

Good ol' Oak Forest, my hometown! This is really just a hodgepodge of pictures from around the area. This very first picture is from Halloween of 2018, when our friend (and my groomsman!) Anthony put together a Halloween party for all of us. It was a BLAST, everyone's costumes were great and we were JAMMIN'!

The next set of photos is Alyssa and I with our Build-a-Bear, Bearald. We sleep with him every night! If one of us is missing from the bed, he's our backup cuddler.

Third set is Alyssa and I in Allie's garage. She was always a great host, so this was a commonplace for us to be found while we were all still in Oak Forest.

Following that is a quick Christmas, actually this past Christmas, at Auntic Dic's! They always have such sparkling decorations, it's hard to pass up the photo op.

Second to last we see a paint-n-sip night we had at Sam and Seans, where I painted a canvas for our lil' animals, PB n' Jams

And last but not least, The Shulls' bridal shower in Midlo! A really sweet yellow-flowery themed bridal shower thrown by a beautiful couple, whose wedding we would attend just a few months later.

This sushi boat was solid but we would later come back here and find old, slimy sushi and steamed rice that clearly was not prepared with rice vinegar. -10/10, would not recommend

In December of 2018, Alyssa and I were pretty close and I wanted to get her a really special gift. Over our time together I found she had a particular interest in wolves... so I got her one! Kind of. Out near Indianapolis there is a wolf sanctuary, "Wolf Park". Here we sponsored a wolf, Timber. I took Alyssa on a trip to Indianapolis which would end with a surprise visit to her birthday gift, a full meet-and-greet with Timber (and fellow wolves at the park).
That weekend we went to the Indianapolis Museum of Art at Newfields, which had a stunning geometric wall we took photos with! Following that we had dinner and a show; we went to see A Christmas Carol at Indianapolis' Civic Theatre. We'd go on to visit Timber a couple more times as the sponsorship lasted a year.

Laugh Factory was a last-second date Alyssa and I put together. We hadn't gone to a stand-up show together before, so we found these tickets on Groupon on a whim. Turned out we'd end up having near-front-row seats next to this nice couple. We chatted with them throughout the show, and then stayed a bit after the show to hangout with them and the comedian, Akeem Woods! He was really friendly and absolutely hilarious.

Lake Geneva is easily one of mine and Alyssa's favorite vacation spots! Unfortunately we only have a picture here from 2019, but out first-ever trip to Lake Geneva was back in 2017, when I was still 20 and therefore not old enough to drink! Ally and I stayed at The Lodge, a spa hotel. Ally got a drink at dinner, while I snuck some sips when the waitress wasn't looking! In hindsight, they probably didn't care, and it was just a silly experience. Since then, we've come back to Lake Geneva to visit The Abbey Resort for another spa vacation, and I'd really highly recommend that place! Alongside your massage, you get a few hours in a relaxing pool area where you can just sit, read, and unwind. We love our spa vacations! We've come here for wine tastings as well -- my favorite "gift wine" was one we found at a small winery, "Sexual Chocolate". It's actually a widely available red wine. If you see a red wine with a bunch of handwritten-looking writing as the label, grab it! it's a delicious red wine to pair with chocolate, and is Advanced Sommelier approved (Thanks Igor!).
Anyways, the pictures you see here are from 2019 at the Ice Castles! Out in Lake Geneva they create a giant castle out of ice, filled with slides and mazes, as well as some drinks and snacks.

Just a quick one here, Mizu Sushi house! We love our sushi boats! This place was really solid, it's in my "C-Tier" which sounds low, but it's definitely a place I'd gladly go back! This tends to be the "All you can eat" category for me, so although the quality isn't S-A-or-B tier, its' still plenty good to eat, and will always satisfy that sushi craving

Out in May of 2019, Ally and I decided to visit Colorado! We chose to check out Colorado Springs, and one of the big attractions out that way is the Royal Gorge Bridge & Park. Royal Gorge is a 1250ft deep canyon just outside of Cañon City. We came here off a suggestion from our friend Pooja who had just gone earlier in the year! The canyon was beautiful and honestly pretty nerve-wracking! The bridge is lined with the flags of all 50 states. Going across the bridge had us holding pretty tight to the railings and nervously looking down. We went on a zipline that went across the gorge, and it was exhilarating! There is also a gondola that goes across the canyon, which you can see us taking pictures in. Lastly, on a lower point of the canyon, is a cave system! We went spelunking and got to see some stalagmites and stalactites. At one point of the tour, they turn off all the lights, and you can't even see your hand in front of your face. Our final stop on our way back to Colorado Springs was an old prison museum, in which they had an old retired gas chamber. Spooky stuff! Right up Ally's alley.

Having flown in-and-out of Denver, we had to hit up the Blue Moon Brewing Company! Blue Moon is my go-to beer, so this was a really cool experience for us. We got to do flights of their experimental beers at the time, and they actually hold a leaderboard of the top-requested beers! I remember here they had been trialing their "Iced Coffee Blonde", which I was excited to see in stores just a few months later for the winter seasonal beers.

The Denver Botanic Gardens was beautiful! We were on our way to the airport when we found we had a few extra hours, so we decided to stop by, and what a great decision that was! We like to visit the botanic gardens of the cities we visit, and this one was my second favorite after Chicago's. They have this large honeycomb-themed pyramid near the center of the garden which is used for research and BEES! We got to see a lot of pretty tulips as they were in-season, and some really wild trees and plants. Denver's Botanic Garden is a great example of placing greenery in a busy city, and always worth the stop.

Our most-anticipated part of this trip, Garden of the Gods! Garden of the Gods is a registered National Natural Landmark with giant spikes of red rock shooting out of the ground. We started off our visit with a Wolf Walk -- again we found an organization which rescued wolves, and this one actually let us walk them! The photos you see are with Colorado Wolf Adventures. These guys were HUGE! Their paws were the size of my face. Still, they acted very similarly to dogs and even let us rub their bellies. After our walk, we went off into the park and got to take some pictures on a light hike through the "garden".
